events.narration: Cells arrive at m1b_cells_in_1 from Module 1's one outlet m1_out_1, already merged (labelled per chamber in Module 1, so they share one line), and fill half of the quench serpentine m1b_mix_1; m1b_waste_1 is vented.
Quench: m1b_quench_in_1 (off-chip selector valve on quench medium) joins the cells at the T-junction and the serpentine mixes it in, neutralising the detach reagent.
Wash the cells into clean buffer fed at m1b_wash_in_1; the old liquid leaves through the vented m1b_waste_1. (Method TBC: DLD array, spiral channel or density cushion.)

Through the depth-weir filter (a 27 um gap under the crest) to the QC window: clumps stay behind, single cells go on. m1b_waste_1 is capped and m1b_buffer_in_1 is vented as the drain; m1b_to_module2_1 stays capped.
Count: with every port capped and the flow stopped, the QC window reads the cell concentration and viability.

Resuspend in dextran buffer fed at m1b_buffer_in_1 (off-chip selector valve on dextran buffer) at the dilution that gives about 0.1 cells per capsule in Module 2; the operator sets it from the count. m1b_to_module2_1 stays capped.

log.message: simulated counter at m1b_qc_window_1: 3,554 cells/uL, 84.3% viable

m1b_resuspend_1 dilution set to 1.82x: counted 3,554 cells/uL at 84% viability; Module 2 makes 1,948,836 capsules/h from 100 uL/h of core stream, so 0.1 cells per capsule needs ~1,949 cells/uL: diluting 1.82x with dextran buffer
cells to Module 2: blocked: viability 84% is below 90% (10x guidance): don't encapsulate these cells
stopped before Module 2: the cells stay in m1b_resuspend_1 for a person to fix (viability 84% is below 90% (10x guidance): don't encapsulate these cells)

scenario.name: m1b_cellprep_low_viability
scenario.description: Too many dead cells: viability under 90%. Dilution can't fix that, so the safety checker blocks the hand-off to Module 2.

reasons: viability 84% is below 90% (10x guidance): don't encapsulate these cells
